newsitem.title: UK: Lloyds Chemists says door open to bidders.
newsitem.headline: Lloyds Chemists says door open to bidders.

text.p: Britain's Lloyds Chemists plc said on Tuesday that it believed that both the rival takeover offers from suitors Unichem Plc and Germany's GEHE AG offered its shareholders more value than the company could achieve alone in the short term.

However, as neither of the two bidders has declared its offer final the Lloyds board said in a statement of formal response to the two approaches that it would continue to advise its shareholders to take no action for the time being.

The company said in a statement that its board had taken into account "that the offers from UniChem and Gehe each provide Lloyds Chemists shareholders with more value than the board believes could be achieved by Lloyds Chemists as an independent company in the immediate future".

It also said it believed that the acquisition represented "a major strategic opportunity for both UniChem and Gehe" and, recognising that neither bidder has declared its offer final, it continued "to advise shareholders to take no action in relation to their shareholdings" for the time being.

In the latest rounds of a long-running takeover race that was interrupted in the spring by the referral of both companies' first bids to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission, UniChem tabled its latest cash and shares offer on October 18.
This deal values Lloyds at 657.6 million pounds, while Gehe's response, launched on November 5, was to offer an all-cash deal of 500p per share that values Lloyds at 650.6 million stg.
Since that bid was launched, Lloyds shares have traded sideways at around 511 pence and were virtualy unchanged at 512p, up 1/2p, by 1100 GMT on Tuesday.
